Segub
sē´gŭb
n. (the youngest son of Hiel, who died when Jericho's gates were set up; also a son of Hezron)
Hebrew Segub, meaning exalted or lifted up — a name whose meaning stands in bitter contrast to what is recorded of the better-known bearer.

Biblical Definition

Five hundred years after Joshua pronounced a curse, a man in Ahab's reign tested it: “In his days did Hiel the Bethelite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun” (1 Kings 16:34). The curse is quoted in Joshua exactly as it fell: “And Joshua adjured them at that time, saying, Cursed be the man before the LORD, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho: he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it” (Joshua 6:26). Hiel lost his eldest at the beginning of the work and his youngest at its completion, and the historian's comment is four words long: according to the word of the LORD. A second and unrelated Segub belongs to the genealogy of Judah: “And afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he married when he was threescore years old; and she bare him Segub” (1 Chronicles 2:21), and “And Segub begat Jair, who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead” (1 Chronicles 2:22).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Segub; the name belongs to the youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite, and to a son of Hezron in the line of Judah.

SEGUB, n. The youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite, who died when the gates of Jericho were set up.

CURSE, n. Malediction; the expression of a wish of evil to another; imprecation of evil, judicially pronounced.

ADJURE, v.t. To charge, bind or command on oath, or under the penalty of a curse.

FOUNDATION, n. The basis or groundwork of anything; that upon which anything stands.

FULFIL, v.t. To accomplish; to perform; to complete; to answer in event what was foretold.

Key Scripture

1 Kings 16:34 — "In his days did Hiel the Bethelite build Jericho: he laid the foundation thereof in Abiram his firstborn, and set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun."

Joshua 6:26 — "And Joshua adjured them at that time, saying, Cursed be the man before the LORD, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho: he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it."

1 Chronicles 2:21 — "And afterward Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he married when he was threescore years old; and she bare him Segub."

1 Chronicles 2:22 — "And Segub begat Jair, who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead."

Modern Corruption

The fulfilment is explained away as a later editorial insertion or as coincidence, and the historian's own explanation of the deaths is set aside.

expand to see more

Historical-critical treatment of 1 Kings 16:34 usually proposes that the notice was composed after the fact to vindicate the curse, or that Hiel's sons died of ordinary causes and the editor supplied the connection. The dictionary rejects that reading. The narrator states the cause plainly — according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Joshua the son of Nun — and the books of Kings are constructed throughout on exactly this principle, tracking prophecies to their fulfilments across centuries. To excise the connection is to remove the thread that holds the book together.

The word itself faces no postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the patience of God's word. Half a millennium separates Joshua's oath from Hiel's building project, and in that interval nothing happened; the curse looked like a dead letter, and a man in the most apostate reign in Israel's history decided to find out. Scripture's consistent testimony is that delay is not cancellation — the Lord is not slack concerning His promise, and the same patience that spared Hiel for years spared him no consequence at the end. A father laid a foundation and buried his firstborn, and finished the gates and buried his youngest, and the historian names the boy.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Segub (H7687), exalted; arar (H779), to curse; shaba (H7650) / alah (H423), an oath or adjuration; dabar YHWH, the word of the LORD.

expand to see more

Hebrew Segub (H7687) — exalted, lifted up; Hiel's youngest son, and a son of Hezron.

Hebrew arar (H779) — to curse; cursed be the man that buildeth this city Jericho.

Hebrew shaba (H7650) — to swear, adjure; Joshua adjured them at that time.

Hebrew bekor (H1060) — firstborn; Abiram, lost at the foundation.

Hebrew debar YHWH (H1697) — the word of the LORD; the stated cause of the deaths.

Usage

"“Set up the gates thereof in his youngest son Segub” — the curse completed."

"“Cursed be the man before the LORD, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho” — spoken five centuries earlier."

"“Segub begat Jair” — the other man of the name, in Judah's line."
